zh: 你能把摄像头重新打开吗？我们看不到你了。
en: Can you bring your camera {back on}? We can't see you.
note: Back on means on again after being off. You can bring, turn, switch or put a camera back on.

zh: 演示结束了，大家可以把摄像头重新打开了。
en: Feel free to {turn|switch|put|bring} your cameras {back on} now the presentation's finished.
note: Turn, switch, put and bring all work with back on for cameras. Back means returning to how it was before.

zh: 抱歉，我刚才是静音状态。
en: Sorry, I was {on mute|muted}.
note: We say someone is on mute, like on hold or on speaker. You can also just say muted.

zh: Mere，你还是静音状态呢。
en: You're still {on mute|muted}, Mere.
note: This is the most common line in any online meeting. On mute describes a state you are in.

zh: 我家狗在叫，我先静音一下。
en: I'm going to {go on mute|mute myself|mute} while my dog's barking.
note: Go on mute means switch your own mic off. Go is used because you move into a new state.

zh: 想发言的时候，别忘了取消静音。
en: Don't forget to {come off mute|unmute|unmute yourself} when you want to speak.
note: Come off mute is the opposite of go on mute. Off shows you are leaving that state.

zh: Tom，你那边突然没声音了。
en: You've {gone quiet|gone silent|cut out} on us, Tom.
note: Gone quiet means we suddenly can't hear you. On us is a friendly way to say it affects the others.

zh: 抱歉，你刚才有一下没声音了，能再说一遍吗？
en: Sorry, you {cut out|dropped out|broke up} for a second there. Can you say that again?
note: Cut out means the sound stopped for a moment. Out shows something disappeared briefly.

zh: 你的声音断断续续的，可能是网络不好。
en: You're {breaking up|cutting out|cutting in and out}. I think your connection's bad.
note: Breaking up means your voice comes in broken pieces. It is the usual phrase for a bad call connection.

zh: 你刚讲到重要的那一页，画面就卡住不动了。
en: Your screen {froze up|froze|locked up} just as you got to the important slide.
note: Froze up means the picture stopped moving completely. Up here means fully or completely.

zh: 几分钟前Aroha从通话里掉线了。
en: Aroha {dropped off|fell off|dropped out of|got kicked off} the call a few minutes ago.
note: Drop off a call means you leave it, usually by accident. Think of the call as something you are on.

zh: Sam好像掉线了，参会名单里已经没有他了。
en: I think Sam's {dropped out|dropped off|left|gone}. His name's disappeared from the list.
note: Dropped out means his connection failed and he left the call without meaning to.

zh: 我得先下线了，两点还有个会。
en: I have to {hop off|jump off|drop off|head off|go|leave} now. I've got another meeting at two.
note: Hop off is a casual way to say leave a call. Hop and jump make it sound quick and easy.

zh: 我们能不能快速通个电话，把这事解决了？
en: Can we {jump on|hop on|get on|have} a quick call to sort this out?
note: Jump on a call means start a short call quickly. A call is something you get on, like a bus.

zh: 我把Sam也拉进通话吧，他清楚细节。
en: Let me {get|bring|pull} Sam {on|onto|into} the call. He knows the details.
note: Get someone on the call means invite them to join it now. We usually say people are on a call.

zh: 现在都有谁上线了？我只看到三个名字。
en: Who's {on|here} so far? I can only see three names.
note: Who's on means who has joined the call. On alone is enough when everyone knows which call you mean.

zh: 你还在线吗？我什么都听不到了。
en: Are you still {on|there|with us}? I can't hear anything.
note: Still on means still connected to the call. Are you still there is another common way to ask.

zh: 抱歉，我正在打另一个电话，结束后给你发消息。
en: Sorry, I'm {on|in} another call. I'll message you after.
note: You are on a call or on the phone. On shows you are busy using that line.

zh: 大家下线以后，你能多留一分钟吗？
en: Can you stay {on|behind} for a minute after everyone else drops off?
note: Stay on means remain in the call after others leave. Stay behind means the same for a room.

zh: 我能插一句吗？我觉得我们漏掉了点东西。
en: Can I just {jump in|cut in|come in|chip in|butt in} here? I think we've missed something.
note: Jump in means start speaking while others are talking. It is a polite, friendly way to interrupt.

zh: 现在我把时间交给Priya，由她来演示。
en: I'll {hand over|pass over|hand it over|pass it over} to Priya now for the demo.
note: Hand over to someone means give them the turn to speak. Over shows the turn moves to another person.

zh: 我说完了，Tom，交还给你。
en: That's all from me, so {back over|back|over} to you, Tom.
note: Back over to you means you return the turn to the person who spoke before you.

zh: 还剩五分钟，我们开始收尾吧。
en: We've got five minutes left, so let's start {wrapping up|winding up|winding down|finishing up}.
note: Wrap up means finish a meeting neatly, like wrapping a present at the end.

zh: 你能两分钟内收个尾吗？三点有人订了这间会议室。
en: Can you {wrap it up|wrap up|finish up} in two minutes? Someone's booked the room at three.
note: Wrap it up asks someone to finish what they are saying soon. It is common when time is short.

zh: 我把幻灯片调出来给大家看。
en: I'll {pull up|bring up|put up|share|open} the deck so everyone can see it.
note: Pull up means open something and show it on screen. Up shows it appears in front of people.

zh: 你能把上一张幻灯片重新调出来吗？
en: Could you bring the previous slide {back up}?
note: Bring back up means show again something that was on screen before. Back means again, up means on screen.

zh: 有问题可以发在聊天框里。
en: Questions can go {in} the chat.
note: We say in the chat, like in a message or in an email. The chat is a space you write in.

zh: 会后我把录像发给大家。
en: I'll {send} the recording {round|around|out} after the meeting.
note: Send round means send to everyone in the group. Round shows it goes to each person in turn.

zh: 你能再往上翻一点吗？刚才第二点我没看清。
en: Can you scroll {back up|up} a bit? I missed the second point.
note: Scroll back up means move up the page to something you already passed. Back means returning.

zh: 好了，我就不耽误你了，谢谢你抽时间。
en: Anyway, I'll {let you go|let you get on|leave you to it}. Thanks for your time.
note: I'll let you go is a polite way to end a call. It sounds like you are freeing the other person.

zh: 谢谢大家，回头见。
en: Thanks, everyone. Catch you {later|soon}.
note: Catch you later is a casual goodbye in New Zealand. It means see you or talk to you later.

zh: 我十分钟后给你回电话。
en: I'll {ring|call|phone} you {back} in ten minutes.
note: Ring someone back means return their call. Ring is the usual word in New Zealand and Britain.

zh: 提醒一下，你的麦克风开着呢，我们能听到你家孩子的声音。
en: By the way, your mic's {on|live}. We can hear your kids.
note: Your mic's on means it is working and people can hear you. Live means the same thing.

zh: 不发言的时候，大家能保持静音吗？
en: Can everyone stay {on mute|muted} unless they're speaking?
note: Stay on mute means keep your mic off. You can go on mute, stay on mute and come off mute.

zh: 今天我就不开摄像头了，可以吗？我网速有点慢。
en: I'll keep my camera {off} today, if that's okay. My internet's slow.
note: Keep something off means leave it switched off. Keep shows it stays that way the whole time.

zh: 抱歉，我刚才被系统踢出了会议。
en: Sorry, I {got kicked out|got booted out|got thrown out|dropped out} of the meeting.
note: Get kicked out means the system removed you without you choosing it. Out shows you left the meeting.

zh: 我的电脑没电了，我用手机重新进会。
en: My laptop's died. I'll {jump back on|hop back on|get back on|come back on|rejoin} from my phone.
note: Jump back on means join the call again. Back means again, on means on the call.

zh: 你能大声一点吗？你声音很小。
en: Can you {speak up|talk louder|speak louder} a bit? You're very quiet.
note: Speak up means talk more loudly. Up here means more, like turn the volume up.

zh: 我先把视频关了，我的网老是断。
en: I'm going to {turn|switch} my video {off}. My connection keeps dropping.
note: Turn off and switch off both mean stop something working. Off is the opposite of on.

zh: 等一下，我把他们从等候区放进来。
en: Hang on, I'll let them {in} from the lobby.
note: Let someone in means allow them to enter. In Teams and Zoom you let people in from the lobby.

zh: 我们挨个做一下自我介绍吧。
en: Let's go {round|around} the room and introduce ourselves.
note: Go round the room means each person takes a turn, one after another. It works online too.

zh: 你能带着我们把这些数字过一遍吗？
en: Could you {talk|walk|take} us {through} the numbers?
note: Talk someone through means explain something step by step. Through shows you go from start to end.

zh: 我能回到Mere刚才说的那一点吗？
en: Can I {jump back|go back|come back|circle back} to what Mere said earlier?
note: Jump back to means return to an earlier point in the conversation. Back means returning.

zh: 抱歉，我跟你抢话了，你先说。
en: Sorry, I {talked over|spoke over|cut across} you. Go ahead.
note: Talk over someone means speak at the same time so they can't be heard. Over shows your voice covers theirs.

zh: 剩下的我们会后单独再聊吧。
en: Let's take the rest of this {offline}.
note: Take something offline means discuss it later outside the meeting, usually with fewer people.

zh: 这个我们最后再回头讨论。
en: Let's come {back to} that at the end.
note: Come back to something means return to a topic later. It is a polite way to pause a topic.

zh: 三点的会还照常开吗？
en: Is the meeting still {on|happening} for three?
note: A meeting that is on is going ahead as planned. A meeting that is off is cancelled.

zh: 抱歉，今天的会不开了，Sam病了。
en: Sorry, today's meeting is {off|cancelled|canceled}. Sam's sick.
note: Off means cancelled when we talk about meetings or plans. On means it is still going ahead.

zh: 抱歉，我刚才走神了一下。
en: Sorry, I {zoned out|spaced out|drifted off} for a second.
note: Zone out means stop paying attention for a while. Out shows your mind went somewhere else.

zh: 你能把音量调大一点吗？视频声音我几乎听不到。
en: Can you {turn|put} the volume {up}? I can hardly hear the video.
note: Turn the volume up means make it louder. Up means more and down means less.

zh: 有回音，谁能把扬声器的音量调小一点？
en: There's an echo. Can someone turn their speakers {down}?
note: Turn something down means make it quieter. Turn it off would mean stop it completely.

zh: 你介意我旁听你们的规划会吗？
en: Do you mind if I {sit in on|listen in on|join} your planning meeting?
note: Sit in on a meeting means attend and listen without being a main part of it.

zh: 抱歉，我们超时了，我长话短说。
en: Sorry, we're {running over|going over|running late}. I'll be quick.
note: Run over means go past the planned finishing time. Over shows you have gone beyond the limit.

zh: 你能把链接丢到聊天框里吗？
en: Could you {pop|put|drop|stick|throw} the link {in|into} the chat?
note: Pop it in the chat is a very common New Zealand way to say post it in the chat.

zh: 刚才有一会儿你断了，不过现在又回来了。
en: We lost you for a bit, but you're {back} now.
note: You're back means we can see and hear you again. Back means returned to how it was.

zh: 现在你的声音非常清楚。
en: You're coming {through} loud and clear now.
note: Come through means your voice or picture reaches the other people. Loud and clear means perfectly.

zh: 抱歉，有人敲门，我两分钟后回来。
en: Sorry, someone's at the door. I'll be {back} in two minutes.
note: Be back means return to where you were. People also say back in two as a short form.

zh: 我们开始吧？人应该都到齐了。
en: Shall we {kick off|get started|start|begin|make a start}? I think everyone's here.
note: Kick off means start, like the start of a football game. It is very common for meetings.

zh: 我得离开一下，马上回来。
en: I need to {step away|step out|pop out|duck out} for a minute. Back soon.
note: Step away means leave your desk or the call for a short time. Away shows you are not there.

zh: 下一个轮到谁？
en: Who's {up} next?
note: Up here means it is your turn, like in sport. You're up means it's your turn to speak.
